explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass), and only for short sequences: L=3 (65% of mass, 47x lift) and L=4 (33%), almost never L=5 and never longer. Within those it depends on what has to be output first: first original token g (50% of mass), r (23%) or 3 (17%), with l and i a weaker tail. For L=4 it also needs a favourable second token (g/r/3/e/h/j/k/y); for L=3 it is more permissive. Strongest activations are L=3 with first token g (e.g. g e j <DEL>, g h j <DEL>). Never fires during the original or copy phases. Activations are tiny (max 0.013). Precision is limited: many short g/r/3-initial sequences do not cross threshold, and which ones do depends on the remaining token content in a way no simple rule captures.
